title: This Plane Is So Quiet It Goes 'Thump' Instead of 'BOOM'!
summary: Imagine a plane that flies faster than the speed of sound but doesn't make that ear-splitting BOOM. That's exactly what NASA's X-59 is built to do! In a new video, the X-59 shows off some dizzying acrobatics over the Mojave Desert. It twists and turns in the sky like a roller coaster. During its latest test on April 14, the plane hit 0.95 Mach — that's about 730 miles per hour. That's almost supersonic, but not quite. Supersonic means faster than the speed of sound. The X-59 is special because when it does go supersonic, it won't create a loud sonic boom. Instead, it will make a quiet 'thump' — about as loud as a car door slamming. That's 16 times quieter than the Concorde, an old supersonic passenger jet. The plane is a team effort between NASA and Lockheed Martin. They've been working on it for over ten years. The goal is to fly at 55,000 feet — way higher than regular planes — and reach Mach 1.4, or about 940 mph. If tests go well, this quiet thump technology could let supersonic planes fly over land again. Right now, they're banned because of the noise. Maybe one day you'll fly across the country in half the time, with just a gentle thump outside your window!
why_it_matters: If quiet supersonic planes become real, you might one day fly across the country in half the time to visit family or go on vacation, with just a soft thump outside your window instead of a scary boom.

background_read: The Concorde (a sleek passenger jet from 1976 to 2003) could cross the Atlantic in under three hours, but its loud sonic booms annoyed people so much that flying faster than sound over land was banned in many countries.
NASA (the U.S. space agency) has been studying ways to quiet sonic booms for decades, because faster travel could save people a lot of time, especially on long flights like New York to Los Angeles.
The Mojave Desert in California is a popular place for testing experimental planes because it is open and far from crowded cities, so noise isn't a big problem.

WHAT: Testing the X-59 plane, which cuts the loud sonic boom down to a gentle thump

WHY: To someday let supersonic planes fly over land again so people can travel much faster

perspectives.description: People who love speed would be thrilled: you could leave after breakfast and arrive in time for lunch, even if the destination is thousands of miles away.
Some people living near airports worry that even a softer thump might still disturb their peace or scare animals, and they think tests need to prove it's really quiet enough.
